<details open>

common, mtmd: bound control vector layer indices and M-RoPE position loops (#31336)

* common: bound control vector layer indices by the model layer count

A direction tensor layer index is parsed from the tensor name with no
upper bound, and the buffer size and write offset are computed in int.
A large index overflows both, so the accumulation writes before the
start of the buffer.

Pass the model layer count to the loader, reject indices above it like
the existing zero index check, and compute the sizes in size_t.

* mtmd: fill M-RoPE positions by whole merge tiles

The position loops of the Qwen-VL, GLM, PaddleOCR and Qwen2.5-VL
encoders hardcode a 2x2 merge inside a stride of n_merge, so a patch
grid that is not a multiple of the merge writes past the positions
buffer.

Abstract: Early AI programs were often also theories of how people think, and programs that wrote programs were, in part, theories of how people program. Here we report on the reanimation of two such programs that offer two seemingly different theories of programming and were developed for quite different purposes. The first, Herbert Simon's Heuristic Compiler (1961), was an experimental model of programming as problem-solving, applying the means-ends analysis methods of the General Problem Solver to investigate the nature of the programming task.
